findings.practical_consequence: A failed corpus adoption can leave a new directive identity active in PostgreSQL with no Qdrant point, while the proposed manifest and rollback proof omit that identity; restoring the files could therefore report failure without actually restoring the pre-adoption corpus state.
evidence: Required behavior: frozen requirement FUT-009 requires a bounded rollback contract across every authoritative consumer, with finite rollback conditions before implementation.

Current producer/degradation path: src/memory_knowledge/workflows/corpus.py:47-48 states that Qdrant failure leaves the entry in PostgreSQL; lines 82-95 write PostgreSQL before Qdrant; lines 116-123 return entry_key only on success and return an error without it after an exception.

Candidate omission: candidate db875fd878e988a7d4e97b5197024836ba7e3d7d620431918ebc6ce4071e365a limits the forward manifest to entry keys returned by successful forward upserts and limits rollback assertions to successfully published forward-only identities.

Downstream incompatibility: src/memory_knowledge/workflows/corpus.py:142-144 documents that deactivation writes PostgreSQL first and a missing Qdrant point errors; the candidate then requires every forward-only identity to exist inactive in both stores and treats missing or mismatched state as failure. That contract cannot converge or prove cleanup for a PostgreSQL-only partial upsert.
